command: set -e; cd /code; yarn --frozen-lockfile; fp="$GRDM_IMAGE|$GRDM_BUILD_RECIPE|$BACKEND|$OSF_URL|$OSF_API_URL|$CAS_URL|$OSF_RENDER_URL|$OSF_FILE_URL|$OSF_HELP_URL|$OSF_COOKIE_DOMAIN"; if [ ! -f /code/dist/index.html ] || [ "$(cat /code/dist/.grdm-build 2>/dev/null)" != "$fp" ]; then echo "ember: building dist for $fp"; rm -rf /code/dist/*; node_modules/.bin/ember build --environment development --output-path /code/dist; node -e "const f='/code/dist/index.html',fs=require('fs');let h=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');h=h.replace(/(name=\x22ember-osf-web\/config\/environment\x22 content=\x22)([^\x22]*)/,(m,a,b)=>{const c=JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(b));c.metricsAdapters=c.metricsAdapters.filter(x=>x.name!=='GoogleAnalytics');return a+encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(c))});fs.writeFileSync(f,h)"; if grep -q GoogleAnalytics /code/dist/index.html; then echo "ember: GoogleAnalytics is still in the built page" >&2; exit 1; fi; printf %s "$fp" > /code/dist/.grdm-build; fi; exec node_modules/.bin/ember serve --path /code/dist --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4200 --live-reload false
note: ember-osf-web's config/environment.js takes its backend URLs from the environment (OSF_URL, OSF_API_URL, OSF_RENDER_URL, OSF_FILE_URL, OSF_HELP_URL, CAS_URL, OSF_COOKIE_DOMAIN); the defaults are localhost:<port> and the retired alias 192.168.168.167:8080 for CAS, so every value is set from the published loopback ports (ADR-02). The prebuilt image runs `ember server`, a full ember-cli build at every start that takes 10+ minutes under amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon and was OOM-killed twice at 6.3 GiB (real install runs 10-12); the command therefore builds once into the named volume ember_osf_web_dist (/code/dist) with a fingerprint in /code/dist/.grdm-build made of the image reference (GRDM_IMAGE = {{SERVICE_IMAGE}}, digest-pinned), the build-recipe version (GRDM_BUILD_RECIPE, bump when this command changes) and the URL settings, and rebuilds only when that fingerprint changes (PR #33 review r1 R1-02: a new image digest must not serve the old bundle), and serves the prebuilt output with `ember serve --path`. Live reload is off (no 41953 port): edit-and-reload of ember sources is not a goal of the prebuilt fallback; it returns with the M4 Dockerfile. JOBS=2 caps ember-cli's parallel build workers; weight 4 and at least 8 GiB cover the build. No depends_on: the container only builds and serves static files (the browser talks to web/api directly), so on a cold start its 13-25 minute build runs in parallel with osf_init and the databases instead of after them (real install run 19). The Google Analytics adapter is deleted from the runtime configuration that ember reads from the meta tag of dist/index.html, right after the build, and the start fails if it is still there: the development build otherwise falls back to the COS property UA-84580271-1, so every developer's browser would call Google (acceptance run 10; app/services/analytics.ts checks that the adapter exists). It is done on dist because the container's /code is read-only and the prebuilt image does not contain RDM-ember-osf-web-dev2027.
